subparts.stem: Write the data set in order, and construct a five-number summary.

mark_breakdown.desc: Identifying median and quartiles from the 19 ordered values

subparts.solution:
The ordered data set has 19 values:
4, 9, 10, 12, 12, 14, 14, 15, 16, **16**, 16, 17, 18, 18, 18, 20, 23, 26, 31
$$\text{median} = 16 \quad (\text{the 10th value})$$
Lower half (first 9 values): 4, 9, 10, 12, **12**, 14, 14, 15, 16 $\Rightarrow Q_1 = 12$
Upper half (last 9 values): 16, 17, 18, 18, **18**, 20, 23, 26, 31 $\Rightarrow Q_3 = 18$

Five-number summary:
$$\text{minimum} = 4, \quad Q_1 = 12, \quad \text{median} = 16, \quad Q_3 = 18, \quad \text{maximum} = 31$$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The five-number summary consists of the minimum, lower quartile ($Q_1$), median, upper quartile ($Q_3$), and maximum.
step_by_step: For $n=19$, the median is the $\frac{19+1}{2} = 10$th value, which is 16.
The lower half contains 9 values; its median ($Q_1$) is the 5th value, which is 12.
The upper half contains 9 values; its median ($Q_3$) is the 15th value, which is 18.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Including the median in the lower and upper halves when $n$ is odd.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Interquartile range is computed as $\text{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Using range (max - min) instead of IQR.

subparts.stem: Calculate the upper and lower boundaries, and hence identify any outliers in the data set.

mark_breakdown.desc: Calculation of upper and lower outlier boundaries using $1.5 \times \text{IQR}$

subparts.solution:
$$\text{upper boundary} = \text{upper quartile} + 1.5 \times \text{IQR} = 18 + 1.5 \times 6 = 27$$
$$\text{lower boundary} = \text{lower quartile} - 1.5 \times \text{IQR} = 12 - 1.5 \times 6 = 3$$
Since 31 is above the upper boundary of 27, 31 is an outlier.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Outlier fences are given by $[Q_1 - 1.5\times\text{IQR}, Q_3 + 1.5\times\text{IQR}]$. Any datum outside this interval is an outlier.
step_by_step: Compare data values to fences: 31 is greater than 27, so it is an outlier.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Using the mean and standard deviation formula instead of quartile fences, or adding $1.5\times\text{IQR}$ to the median.

subparts.stem: Draw a box plot to represent the data.

mark_breakdown.desc: Drawing box from $Q_1=12$ to $Q_3=18$ with vertical line at median 16
Whiskers extending to minimum (4) and largest non-outlier value (26), with outlier 31 plotted as an isolated point

subparts.solution:
Draw a number line from 0 to 35.
- Lower whisker extends to the minimum value: 4.
- Box begins at $Q_1 = 12$, has median marked at 16, and ends at $Q_3 = 18$.
- Upper whisker extends to the largest non-outlier value: 26.
- The outlier at 31 is plotted as an individual point/asterisk.

ai_explanation.concept_rule: In a modified boxplot, whiskers extend to the smallest and largest values that are not outliers, while outliers are plotted as individual points.
step_by_step: Plot the box with boundaries at $Q_1=12$ and $Q_3=18$.
Mark the median at 16 with a vertical line.
Draw the left whisker from 12 to 4.
Draw the right whisker from 18 to 26 (the largest value $\le 27$).
Mark the outlier at 31 with an asterisk or dot.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Extending the whisker all the way to 31 instead of stopping at 26.
